steps.text: An electric cell is a small source of electricity with two ends called terminals. Let's find them.
Tap the “Positive (+)” terminal to highlight it.
Every cell has a positive terminal (the metal cap, marked +) and a negative terminal (the flat base, marked −).
Current flows out of the + terminal and back into the − terminal. Getting the terminals right is how you connect a cell into a circuit.

coach.mission: Identify the positive and negative terminals of a cell.
whenStuck: The metal cap is the + terminal; the flat base is the − terminal.
Tap a terminal to highlight and check it.
whenWrong: The raised metal cap is positive (+); the flat end is negative (−).
Look for the + and − marks on the cell.
whenCorrect: Good — + is the cap, − is the base.
coach.done: You've identified a cell's terminals. Explore more, or move on when you're ready.
